recipes.name: Chile Relleno Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 (4 ounce) cans whole green chile peppers, drained

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine ground beef and onions in a large skillet over medium-high heat; cook and stir until browned, about 5 to 7 minutes; drain excess fat.

Arrange 1 can of chile peppers on the bottom of a 7x11-inch baking dish. Sprinkle with half of the cheese and top with meat mixture. Sprinkle meat mixture with remaining cheese, followed by next can of chile peppers.
Combine eggs, flour, and milk in a medium bowl, whisking until smooth; pour into baking dish over chile peppers. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 to 50 minutes. Let cool briefly before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Chile Relleno Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This chile rellenos casserole made with layers of ground beef and green chile peppers is an easy version of the classic Mexican stuffed peppers.

video.description: Instead of stuffing peppers, we’re stuffing a casserole dish with this easy weeknight dinner recipe! In this video, Natalie shows you how to make a Chile relleno casserole using charred poblano peppers, enchilada sauce, and heaps of gooey melted cheese. Layered with the peppers, cheese, and sauce, this simple casserole is packed with comforting flavor that the whole family will enjoy.

review.reviewBody: I have been using a version of this recipe for years. For the milk I use a 14 oz can of evap. milk only. I live alone so I make the casserole in mini-loaf pans and freeze, then thaw and heat when I want it later.

Just looking at this recipe, I could tell it would be WAY too bland for our tastes, as other reviewers noted. To liven it up and make it a 5* recipe, add a packet of taco seasoning, 2 tsp fresh garlic, a Tbsp of chile sauce, and some black pepper. I also used monterey-jack cheese and added chili powder to the top. Excellent with changes!

Loved it!! I usually try to follow a recipe closely on the first try, but I did make some changes to this based on other reviews. I added about 1/3 packet of taco seasoning to the meat, and some pepper jack cheese to the casserole. This may not be authentic Mexican, and may not taste exactly like chili rellenos, but it's darn good and I will be making it again!

I'm not sure if anyone mentioned this yet. So here goes!

Buy fresh greenchiles, anaheim will do- But Hatch are best.. Roast them in your oven broiler till they blister, turning to get all sides even as possible. Remove and place in a brown grocery bag, with the top folded over for 5 or so minutes. Peel stem and seed. 

The other tip is to combine your ground beef with an equal ammount of PORK CHIORIZO. Brown them together. Make sure you cook thoroghly. Drain grease and continue with original recipe.

I also replace a small (1/3 portion) of the flour measure for the casserole "glue" with yellow corn meal, and add a few shakes of any mexican brand or tabaso type sauce to the batter.

Fight Night Favorite!
Great if you add lots of cumin, chili powder, oregano and garlic powder.

Put it this way: My 11 year-old had five helpings! And then two days later asked when I was going to make it again. Since I used a 9 x 13 dish, I altered the recipe by using 3 cans of chiles and 2 cups of cheese. I also sauted the beef with taco seasoning - couldn't imagine the dish without the seasoning.

I made this and replaced the beef w/ bacon that I diced and fried up quickly. I used 1 can diced green chiles and 1 can diced jalapenos because we like some heat. I served it for breakfast with toast and sliced tomatoes broiled w/ a little cheese on top. It was really good, but even BETTER later, reheated, between two slices of buttered toast as a sandwich. Maybe not traditional but one of the best breakfast sandwiches I've had! I sliced the leftovers into 'sandwich size' and froze to have quick breakkies!

SO, SO =-(
For a traditional taste & better visuals:
Break up a 14.5oz can of Mexican Style Stewed tomatoes w/fork and empty into the baking dish.
I used 6 Broiled/peeled/seeded Poblano peppers. Added garlic, oregano, salt & pepper to stuffing, carefully stuffed the peppers, placed on the tomato sauce.
In a bowl Whisk: 6 eggs, 1/3C flour, 1ts B.Powder & Pinch of salt, and pour over the sauce/peppers, sprinkle w/1C of shredded cheese and bake. GORGEOUS DISH!

Loved this dish! I used 6 fresh poblano peppers in place of canned. Roasted peppers in the oven till charred, steamed in plastic bag for 20 minutes and removed the skin and seeds. Added some chili powder and cumin to season the chorizo as well as 1 pound of pulled pork mixed together. Had two guests for dinner who both loved this dish too! Will definitely make again.
Pretty good dish! Seems more like a spicy breakfast meal than one eaten at lunch but we still liked it. Also, add the taco seasoning to the meat...it really does the trick!

I made some changes to the recipe. Instead of hamburger I used Jimmy Dean's Chorizo. A one pound chub. It was on sale for $1.99, so a lot cheaper than hamburger. I also used two 7 oz cans of diced green chiles. First I sprayed a casserole dish with Pam spray. I spooned in one can of green chiles. Sauteed half a diced onion with some garlic. Cooked the chorizo with the onion and garlic, and added 1 1/2 cups of cooked rice to the mixture. Spooned half the mixture onto the green chiles, spread pepper jack cheese on top. Spooned the other half onto the cheese. Spread more cheese onto that. Put the other can of green chiles into a blender with 4 eggs, 1/4 cup of flour and 1 cup of milk. Blended on low for a minute then poured on top of the chorizo mixture. Put rest of the cheese on top. Baked at 350 for 50 minutes. Made some homemade refried beans for a side. That was a good dinner. Plus leftovers for work.
Delicious
Husband loved it. Used 2 fresh chile rellanos, larger chop.

Chiles Rellenos are my favorites and this rendition in the form of a casserole is excellent. I usually do not make rellenos at home because it can get messy. This is not messy at all but just as satisfying as the real thing. Highly recommend. It is worth the try.
No hamburger in the video? I also skipped it and used charred poblano peppers. Turned out great

I was shocked - so many wonderful reviews but this was not at all good. It was bland with no flavor and after really looking at the ingredients it should have been a heads up. My only change was using a can of chilies instead of whole ones which doesn't make up for no flavor in the other layers.
So simple and tasty! Followed as written. Tasted like breakfast casserole meets chile rellenos. Mine was cooked in 40 minutes.
Improvised used fresh peppers, roasted, peeled, and diced. JD Sausage, layered shred Mex cheese, 1/4 c cornbread mix, garlic granules, cumin, pepper mix. Then the 4 eggs and milk
YUM DELICIOUS!!
I made it, it was great! I seasoned the ground beef a little with cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, and of course salt and pepper. Thanks for posting this recipe.
